title: Introduce holistic fallback meter and regional venting gate
author: Priya Srinivasan
body:
Summary: Adds a lightweight fallback-meter and a regional venting gate to reduce noisy circuit flips and to provide a gentle, observable path for regional load venting during transient SLO pressure. This PR bundles a small runtime control, a routing policy integration, telemetry hooks, and a controlled rollout plan.

Why: Over the last quarter we saw multiple incidents where regional bursts triggered aggressive circuit breaks and immediate tenant evictions; restoring stability required manual intervention and led to customer-visible tail latency spikes. The fallback-meter provides an amortized view of fallback events per-region per-tenant, allowing the control-plane to apply graduated venting instead of immediate hard-cut evictions. The venting gate implements a soft admission taper that reduces allowed fastpath requests from affected regions while preserving slowpath/backoff routes and KV cache preservation where possible.

Design: 1) fallback_meter: an in-memory sliding-window counter with decayed weights (configurable window=5m, decay=exp with half-life=60s). The meter exposes TTLed snapshots surfaced to the control-plane via existing telemetry bridge. 2) venting_gate: admission controller in routing layer that consults configured policy (region budgets, tenant weights, SLO penalties) and the fallback_meter. It supports three modes: monitor-only, soft-vent (probabilistic reject/redirect), hard-vent (force-evict). Default rollout will keep monitor-only enabled and soft-vent available behind a feature flag. 3) policy config: new YAML schema under runtime/policies/venting.yaml with guardrails for tenant fairness, retries, and KV-preservation hints. 4) Telemetry: adds metrics (fallback_meter.count, venting_gate.rate_reduction, venting_gate.mode_change) and tracing annotations to correlate with SLO breaches.

What changed (high level): - runtime/eviction/fallback_meter.go: new meter implementation and tests - runtime/routing/venting_gate.go: admission logic and unit tests - controlplane/policies/venting.yaml.example: policy schema and examples - telemetry/metrics_registry.go: new metrics registration and dashboards links - docs/observability/venting.md: operator guide and rollback steps - integrations/linear/ENG-3421.md: linked runbook snippets - tests/e2e/venting_scenarios.yaml: synthetic scenario harness

Rollout plan: 1) Feature flag gate.default=monitor-only on main for 48h in canary region (us-west-2). 2) Enable soft-vent with conservative default policy (max 10% fastpath reduction, per-tenant caps) in canary for 24h while monitoring fallback_meter.count and latency SLOs. 3) If stable, expand soft-vent to all regions with 1% increments per region per hour. 4) Hard-vent only enabled by SRE on-call for emergency evacuations and tied to an explicit escalation key.

Observability and alerts: New SLO-linked alert SRE.VENTING_HIGH_RATE (threshold: fallback_meter.count > 50/min sustained for 3m) and dashboard panels for per-region venting_heatmap. We emit structured events for mode transitions so audit logs can reconstruct actions.

Backout: Revert feature flag to disable venting_gate or set gate.mode=monitor-only. Control-plane supports a fast override to set per-region policy to "passthrough". A rollback playbook is included in docs/observability/venting.md.

Testing: Unit + integration + e2e harness that simulates regional QPS spikes and KV cache pressure. Canary run in us-west-2 performed with synthetic tenants; results show a 42% reduction in immediate eviction events and no measurable degradation in median latency.

Security: No auth model change. Policy files validated by existing schema validator. No secrets handled.

Related: ENG-3421 (linear) contains the long-form proposal and requirements. SUP-78 is the customer incident that motivated the soft-vent path.

Checklist:
- [x] New runtime components covered by unit tests
- [x] Integration tests for routing + meter
- [x] Metrics and dashboards added
- [x] Canary rollout plan and rollback instructions
- [x] Runbook snippets linked

Notes: This is intended to be low-risk (monitor-only by default). The implementation favors observability and conservative defaults. We intentionally do not change existing eviction heuristics; the venting gate operates as a pre-admission filter and delegates to existing eviction paths only when policy escalates to hard-vent.

review_comments: Marco Alvarez: Can we make the meter window configurable per-region? Concerned about noisy regions driving global policy.
Author (Priya): Yes — added region_override in policy schema and tests to validate per-region windows (see venting.yaml.example).
Hannah Li: The soft-vent probabilistic algorithm needs to be seedable for reproducible tests.
Author (Priya): Added deterministic seeding for test harness and logged seed value when feature_flag.test_mode=true.
Samir Patel: Add a guard to avoid double-counting fallbacks when multiple routers in the same request path annotate the event.
Author (Priya): Implemented an idempotency tag on the tracing span and a simple de-duplication in fallback_meter.ingest().

release_notes: Adds a monitor-first fallback meter and a controllable regional venting gate to provide gradual, observable load venting under SLO pressure. Ships with conservative defaults and a canary rollout plan.
post_merge_actions: Enable monitor-only mode in us-west-2 (feature flag) and watch venting_gate.metrics for 48h
Create dashboard shortcut in SRE home view: Observability / Venting Gate
Schedule follow-up: ENG retrospective and policy tuning session (ENG-3421)
If anomalies: rollback by toggling feature flag or applying passthrough policy
